implementerProof.how: Its three entries were re-run here, not read, and each with the previous head's bundle beside it in the same run: the listener answering HTML under a 200, the file faces, and the smoke. I drove two cases beyond them that the architect asked for — a listener answer of valid JSON that misses the schema, and the interests reconciliation observed on the registry rather than inferred — and both hold. The behaviour of this round is right. The round fails on the push that carried it, below, which is not a behaviour of the code.

failures.criterion: Every code push of this pull request starts the repository's checks, and the head that merges has CI (skill://legion-worker, 'Every role pushes its own commits': a handoff-only push carries skip-checks: true, every other push carries no such line, and a head with no CI is refused at READY).
failures.evidence: The branch head e7fdeea43528f8c0227d6562788845fa244eda89 ends with 'skip-checks: true' after two empty lines — read with git log -1 --format=%B e7fdeea43528 | cat -A — and the push it headed carried a code commit, 301288e631cb, holding packages/claude-envoy/src/envoy-channel-server.ts, src/session-identity.ts, tests/envoy-channel-handoff.test.ts and the rebuilt dist. GitHub therefore started nothing: `gh pr checks 2154` lists one check, pr-title; `gh run list --commit e7fdeea43528f8c0227d6562788845fa244eda89` holds only PR Title runs, which come from pull_request events rather than from the push; and `gh run list --commit 301288e631cb` is empty. main's required set is lint, typecheck, test and pr-title, so three required checks have never run on this round's code. No red test can pin this: it is a property of the push, not of the source. The remedy is a head whose message carries no trailer — a rewrite of e7fdeea43528's message and a force-push, or any later push whose head carries none. This handoff's own push is handoff-only and so carries the trailer, which is right for it and does not cure the code head.

failureInContext.theRemedyIsSound: The three faces the reviewer and the architect named were all driven here and all hold, each with the previous head's bundle beside it in the same run. What fails is how this round was delivered, not the boundary move: the implementer should not read the verdict as the change being wrong.
failureInContext.secondOfItsClass: This is the second defect of one shape in this issue, and the retro learning should carry the two together rather than as two incidents. In round four a code commit kept the review App as its author because handoff_complete guards the handoff commit of a push and nothing guards the code commit beside it. Here a trailer meant for a handoff-only push rode a push that also carried code, so GitHub started nothing for the code. Both are a rule that is right for one of the two commits in a push and silently wrong for the other, and in both the wrong half is the code commit — the half that matters most and is checked least.

proof.criterion: The reviewer's defect, listener face: an answer that is not JSON must not cost the session its role, and must be queued so a heartbeat takes the role back.
proof.surface: The committed dist/envoy-channel.js run as Claude Code runs it, against a real nats-server with JetStream and an Envoy listener built from this tree, behind a proxy of mine that shapes the first POST /v1/roles/set. Two shapes: an HTML body under a 200, which the real client parses at packages/envoy-client/src/transport.ts:395, and a 200 carrying valid JSON the role answer's schema rejects.
proof.command: a tester probe (/tmp/r5-role.sh with /tmp/r5-proxy.ts, deleted after the round), cases L1 and L3, with the holder read from the listener's own GET /v1/roles/planner
proof.observed: HTML under a 200: the session alive, one stderr line 'envoy-channel: could not restore the role (JSON Parse error: Unrecognized token "<"); the next heartbeat retries' — naming no file, because no file was at fault — and the listener then answering holder=l1-head with the record kept. Valid JSON missing the schema: the same, holder=l3-head. So a ZodError from the wire is queued, which is the half the remedy had to separate.
proof.negativeControl: The previous head's bundle, d4de531733a9, in the same run against the same proxy: 'could not restore the role from <…>/roles/l2-base.json (JSON Parse error: Unrecognized token "<"); the session starts without one' — blaming a role file that was good — and the holder still empty after twelve seconds. The same for the schema miss at l4-base. That is the defect reproduced and the fix beside it.

proof.criterion: The file face has not widened: only bytes that will never parse suppress the retry, and every other failure to read the record is queued.
proof.surface: The same live rig with no proxy refusals, one role record per case.
proof.command: the same probe, cases F1 to F5: truncated bytes, JSON that misses the schema, no record at all, the record at mode 000, and a directory standing where the record should be
proof.observed: Truncated bytes: one line, 'the role record <…>/roles/f1-trunc.json cannot be parsed (JSON Parse error: Unterminated string); the session starts without a role', the role never claimed over ten seconds, no retry line. JSON missing the schema ({"session_id":"f2-schema","role":5}): the same suppression, naming the field — the file-side ZodError, the other half of the separation. No record: no line at all. Mode 000: 'could not restore the role (EACCES: permission denied, open …); the next heartbeat retries'. A directory in its place: the same with EISDIR. Each of the five left the session alive, and none wrote a second line: the startup catch marks the run reported, so the heartbeat's own retry does not repeat it.
proof.negativeControl: The two suppressed cases against the two queued ones in the same probe and the same rig: identical plumbing, opposite outcomes, so what decides is the origin of the failure and not the rig. The previous head's bundle, which suppressed a wire SyntaxError as well, is the control in the other direction.

proof.criterion: A queued role retry must not stop the heartbeat's interests reconciliation, including the adoptHandoff path.
proof.surface: The same rig: the proxy answering every POST /v1/roles/set with 503 so the retry fails on every tick, and refusing the first GET /v1/interests/<session> so the startup read fails, with the session's interests in the registry changed under it while it runs.
proof.command: the same probe, cases R1 and R3: a topic added to the registry that the session does not follow, then the registry read back from the listener over the next heartbeats
proof.observed: With the claim failing every tick, the registry went from notifications.agent.r3-head, notifications.probe.drifted, notifications.probe.kept to notifications.agent.r3-head, notifications.probe.kept — the reconciliation removed the drifted topic and kept the followed one — and no 'registry heartbeat failed' line was written at all. So the tick ran past transferRole to syncRegisteredInterests on every beat while the role kept failing.
proof.negativeControl: The previous head's bundle in the same shape: the drifted topic was still in the registry after two more heartbeats, and 'envoy-channel: registry heartbeat failed (POST …/v1/roles/set failed with 503 …); retrying every heartbeat' was written once — the tick ending at transferRole, which is the starvation this change removes. One honest limit of the rig: a message published to a topic the registry lists reached the session on both heads, so delivery does not discriminate here — the listener fans out server-side. The registry drift is what does.

notProven: That Claude Code itself sends session_title, and that the daemon's seeded '/rename Legion <role> · <KEY>' makes a pane read as its role and issue: Claude Code cannot run in a Legion issue pod, so every hook payload in every run here is JSON the harness writes in the documented shape.

The webkit, webkit-iphone, firefox and firefox-download-navigation projects: Playwright's host validation refuses to start those engines in this pod for want of system libraries no agent can install without root. CI carries them — and at this head CI has not run at all.
A session whose Envoy or inbound messages are off stamps its title once at startup, so a later rename does not reach its Dispatch attribution. Unchanged behaviour for every title, not this change's.
